diff --git a/requirements.txt b/requirements.txt
index 3f1c2a4..8b7e9d1 100644
--- a/requirements.txt
+++ b/requirements.txt
@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 fastapi==0.110.0
 uvicorn==0.29.0
 pydantic==2.6.4
 requests==2.31.0
 PyYAML==6.0.1
+orjson==3.10.0
diff --git a/app/webhooks.py b/app/webhooks.py
index 9a7d3e2..c41f0b8 100644
--- a/app/webhooks.py
+++ b/app/webhooks.py
@@ -1,20 +1,21 @@
 import hashlib
 import hmac
-import json
 import os

+import orjson
+
 WEBHOOK_SECRET = os.environ["WEBHOOK_SECRET"].encode()


-def verify_signature(body: str, signature: str) -> bool:
-    expected = hmac.new(WEBHOOK_SECRET, body.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
-    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)
+def verify_signature(body: bytes, signature: str) -> bool:
+    expected = hmac.new(WEBHOOK_SECRET, body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
+    return expected == signature


-def parse_payload(body: str) -> dict:
+def parse_payload(body: bytes) -> dict:
     """Parse a webhook payload from the request body."""
-    return json.loads(body)
+    return orjson.loads(body)


 def event_type(payload: dict) -> str:
     return payload.get("action", "unknown")
diff --git a/app/routes.py b/app/routes.py
index 5e2b7a1..0d93f4c 100644
--- a/app/routes.py
+++ b/app/routes.py
@@ -8,10 +8,10 @@ router = APIRouter()

 @router.post("/webhooks/github")
 async def github_webhook(request: Request):
-    body = (await request.body()).decode()
+    body = await request.body()
     signature = request.headers.get("X-Hub-Signature-256", "").removeprefix("sha256=")
     if not verify_signature(body, signature):
         raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="bad signature")
     payload = parse_payload(body)
     background.enqueue(event_type(payload), payload)
     return {"ok": True}

claims.concern: Signature check switched from hmac.compare_digest to ==, which leaks timing and lets an attacker forge webhook signatures byte by byte.
orjson is a new native-code dependency added to the request path with no review of its supply chain.

messages.text: Blocking. Line 12 replaces a constant-time compare with ==, which opens a timing attack on webhook signatures. On top of that, orjson is a new compiled dependency sitting directly on untrusted input.

claims.concern: orjson.loads parses large webhook payloads roughly 3x faster than json.loads on this hot path.
Dropping the .decode() avoids an extra full copy of every request body.

messages.text: Approve. Parsing raw bytes with orjson removes a decode copy and speeds up the busiest endpoint we have. This is exactly the latency fix we needed.

claims.concern: parse_payload changed from str to bytes, so any caller still passing a str will now fail.
verify_signature changed from str to bytes; same risk for any other caller.

messages.text: Blocking. Two public functions changed their argument type from str to bytes. The diff updates app/routes.py, but nothing proves that is the only caller.

claims.concern: verify_signature and parse_payload changed behavior with no tests added or updated.

messages.text: The change is small and readable, but no tests come with it. I want a test for both changed functions before merge.
Approve. This is the webhook latency fix we promised for this release, and the diff is tightly scoped to it.

claims.concern: The switch to == has nothing to do with the speedup and should be reverted.

messages.text: Security is right about line 12, and I missed it. Reverting to hmac.compare_digest costs nothing, so I am moving to approve_with_changes. But orjson is pinned at line 6 and widely deployed. Blocking on it throws away a 3x speedup over a hypothetical.

Performance made a fair point. orjson is pinned to an exact version, so the supply-chain risk is bounded and I withdraw my block on it. I move to approve_with_changes on one condition: line 12 goes back to compare_digest.

claims.concern: Shipping a breaking signature change with no shim means one missed caller becomes a production outage.

messages.text: Product says the diff is tightly scoped, but changing a function signature is never local. Unless parse_payload also accepts str, I stay at block.

The only caller in this diff, app/routes.py line 11, was updated, so Compatibility is guarding against code we can't see. I agree with Security's one-line fix and move to approve_with_changes, but holding the release for a speculative caller is not worth it.

A str | bytes shim in parse_payload would satisfy me, and I'd approve with that change. It isn't in this diff, though, and nobody has confirmed there are no other callers, so I stay at block at lower confidence.

claims.concern: A security-sensitive regression got this far precisely because verify_signature has no test.

messages.text: Security's finding changes my view. A test would have caught the == regression, so this is evidence of a gap, not a style nit. I am moving from approve_with_changes to block until verify_signature has a test.

Fair hit from Quality. I'd accept one test for verify_signature added to this PR, but not a full test suite. If that still isn't enough for Compatibility and Quality, a human should make the ship call.

resolved: Signature check must stay constant-time: all agents agree to restore hmac.compare_digest at app/webhooks.py line 12.
orjson as a new dependency is acceptable because it is pinned to an exact version (Security withdrew its block after Performance's argument).
unresolved: compatibility vs product: parse_payload's str-to-bytes change may break callers outside this diff. Either ship now and audit later, or add a str | bytes shim first.
quality vs product: merge with only a verify_signature test, or hold the release until both changed functions are covered.
human_decisions: Are there callers of parse_payload or verify_signature outside app/routes.py (background jobs, other services) that still pass str?
Is shipping the webhook latency fix in this release worth merging security-sensitive code with minimal test coverage?
